report.summary: The release expands interactive prompt handling across browser and terminal experiences and improves status and message feedback.
keyChanges: Browser-created instances now provide browser dialogs by default: confirmation prompts use a confirm dialog, while every other prompt type uses a plain text prompt; selection options, placeholders, and initial values are not applied by that handler.
Browser instance configuration can supply its own prompt handler or reporter instead of the defaults, and prompt calls without a configured handler fail with a clear unsupported error.
Text prompts display the placeholder when the current value is empty, including when showing validation errors or submission.
Confirmation prompts default to Yes, with the initial answer set to true unless explicitly supplied; multi-select prompts require at least one choice unless configured otherwise.
Option prompts now display labels, hints, selection and cancellation states, and grouped-option structure; prompt status symbols also vary by state.

The primary entry point now creates loggers with environment-based log-level and reporter defaults, accepts partial overrides, and attaches a prompt capability; the shared entry point no longer re-exports the logger creator.
The new prompt capability supports text input, confirmation, single selection, and multiple selection; string choices are presented as both labels and values, and multiple selection can be optional.
Messages now display the first line beside its status symbol and subsequent lines on separate, aligned lines; an empty message displays only the vertical divider.
Selection prompts display available options, highlight the active choice, and show a selected or cancelled result.

Spinner messages remove one to three trailing periods while running, then replace the animation with the supplied completion message; error, information, step, success, and warning messages use distinct symbols and colors.
Terminal messages and notes use colored status symbols, with Unicode or ASCII symbols selected for terminal support.
Password prompts accept a custom mask or use the default bullet mask, and show masked values in submitted or canceled states.
Grouped prompts run in order; when cancellation occurs and a callback is supplied, the canceled result is recorded, the callback runs, and prompting continues.
Notes remove ANSI escape sequences when measuring message width so color codes do not count as visible text.

report.summary: The release changes how the editor updates, restores, and recovers drawing data.
keyChanges: Deleting selected elements now returns the remaining elements instead of only mutating the original list, allowing delete and cut actions to retain unselected elements in the drawing.

Moving selected elements one step or to the front or back now returns the reordered elements, allowing each layer-order action to retain the updated drawing. Other selection-helper changes do not alter runtime behavior.
Clearing selection now returns the drawing’s updated element list, so Escape, clicking an empty area, and pasting no longer discard the list while clearing selection.

Undo and redo now apply returned snapshots and treat an unavailable history entry as no result; malformed snapshots are ignored instead of throwing, while normal undo and redo should still restore drawings. Rendering, export, saving, and scrollbar changes only accept read-only inputs and do not change runtime behavior.
On startup, saved drawing elements are now restored separately from saved editor settings, including when no settings are available.
Deleting selected elements and undoing or redoing now apply the returned drawing data, so these actions can update the visible scene.
Keyboard movement, layer ordering, selection, and style pasting now assign updated drawing data; the supplied code does not establish a different visible result for these operations.
Pasting no longer subtracts the copied group’s minimum x and y coordinates before positioning it, so content copied from nonzero coordinates can land offset from the paste target.
Shift-clicking an empty canvas area now preserves the current selection; previously, that action cleared it.
Selected-object deletion and saved-scene loading now adopt the returned drawing list, so verify the displayed drawing reflects those updates.
Drawing-element collections are now typed as read-only, and new scenes still start with an empty collection; no user-visible behavior changes are evidenced.
Importing a valid JSON file without an elements field now produces an empty scene; previously, the existing drawing was left unchanged.
Unreadable JSON imports now resolve with an empty scene instead of failing during parsing.
When saved drawing data is valid but saved interface-state data is invalid, the drawing is now retained; previously, both were discarded.
Restored elements keep the same defaults for missing IDs, fill style, stroke width, roughness, and opacity; the export change only affects accepted input types, not exported content.

The new value lookup treats zero as missing: for example, zero opacity can fall through to the 100 default, and zero sloppiness may no longer appear as a selected setting.
The color picker now types an absent color as null rather than undefined; the supplied changes do not alter runtime behavior.

report.summary: The release changes how text is sized, positioned, and displayed across the whiteboard and exports.
keyChanges: Text height now uses 1.2 times the font size per line, and width measurement normalizes carriage-return line breaks; text dimensions and placement can therefore differ from the previous browser-based measurements.

A word whose measured width exactly matches the available line width is now kept intact instead of entering the old character-breaking path, and bound text is explicitly wrapped before its dimensions are recalculated.
New standalone text no longer receives the previous baseline-based upward offset, so its starting position changes when created on empty canvas.
Canvas rendering now positions text lines using a bottom text baseline, and SVG rendering no longer offsets text using its saved baseline; restored text and exports may therefore align differently.
Resizing text and shapes with attached text now scales font size from width and no longer recalculates the text baseline, changing how labels may sit after a resize or flip.
While editing text attached to a shape or connector, the editor now sizes its height from measured text on every input, including single-line text.
The text editor now uses the text element’s width directly rather than capping it to the available width; Firefox and Safari add 0.5 pixels to that width.

Confirm a single word whose measured width exactly equals the available inner width stays whole on one line and is not split into characters.
Validate that bound text reaching the shape’s available width wraps without clipping and that the text and shape dimensions still accommodate the text.
Verify that clicking empty canvas at (200,200) and entering “QA” creates standalone text without the previous baseline-based upward shift from the clicked position.
Check that unbinding text from a shape leaves the text readable and positioned within its text box.
Confirm that loading the legacy drawing keeps its text visible and that the saved baseline no longer determines text-line placement.
Validate that the text remains legible and within its text box in canvas rendering and in both PNG and SVG exports.
Verify that resizing a shape with multi-line bound text by dragging a corner changes the label font size with the resized width and leaves the label visible and attached.
Check that flipping a shape or connector with bound text leaves its text visible and attached.
Confirm that dragging a connector point or resizing its container updates the wrapped bound label without clipping it.
Verify that editing bound text and deleting content until only one line remains updates the editor height without a visible jump.
Check that editing the unbound text wider than the visible canvas area remains usable, including in Firefox or Safari where supported.

report.summary: The release makes editing and connecting arrows in diagrams more intuitive and responsive.
keyChanges: Dragging an arrow focus point now recalculates both the dragged endpoint and any other bound endpoint, so verify the arrow stays connected during focus-point edits.
Dragging an interior point of a multi-point arrow now also recalculates its bound endpoints even when neither endpoint is selected, so verify the route changes without losing its connections.
Arrow attachment calculations now use shared element-center geometry, and endpoint updates no longer avoid rectangular corners; verify connections near shape corners and on positioned shapes.
Arrow endpoints and elbow-arrow endpoints now pass a numeric binding distance to shape hit detection, affecting whether nearby shapes are found while dragging.
The element package now exports arrow-focus and arrow-interaction helpers, and the public types expose the App type; these are integration API additions, not established changes to the canvas UI.

Selected, bound two-point arrows can show circular focus points and dashed connectors at valid binding locations; hovering a focus point highlights it, and hover and pointer-down detection use a radius of 1.5 times the focus-point size divided by the current zoom.

The hovered-point highlight is now suppressed while a linear-element point is actively being dragged. Focus points are not shown for elbow arrows, arrows with other than two points, or when binding is disabled.

Dragging an arrow focus point can attach it to a nearby shape, switch between inside and orbit binding modes with Alt, or detach it when moved onto empty canvas; overlapping candidates are resolved using front-to-back order and a distance-or-inside check.
A direct click on an arrow focus point is now recognized even without a preceding pointer move, and releasing the drag updates the shape’s arrow connection.
Hovering over a focus point on a connected arrow now shows a pointer cursor, indicating that point can be interacted with.
Pressing or releasing Alt now invokes arrow point-drag handling; test Alt-modified editing of a connected arrow alongside the existing binding-mode interaction.

report.summary: The release improves drawing selection and frame-based output while expanding editor preferences and refining controls.
keyChanges: Box selection now accounts for stroke width and attached arrow text, clips to visible frame contents, and can select intersecting outlines in overlap mode; previously it required the element bounds to be fully enclosed.
Pointer hit testing for selected elements now follows a rotated element’s actual bounds rather than its larger axis-aligned bounding box, making clicks on empty corners behave differently.

Curve checks for free-draw and line strokes can now use up to 10 solver iterations instead of 4, so intersections that previously needed more solving steps may now be detected during canvas interactions.
Point-derived bounds can now expand by an optional padding amount; calls that omit padding retain their previous bounds.
New drawings default to box selection mode “contain”; scene restoration now keeps a saved “overlap” or “contain” preference, so selection mode may differ from older drawings or saved settings.
Frame-based canvas and SVG exports now calculate which elements overlap a frame using a map of the scene’s elements, which may change what appears in exports near frame boundaries.

Multi-selection bounds now extend by twice the transform-handle spacing at the current zoom, and the pointer shows a move cursor over that padded area; Alt+Ctrl or Alt+Cmd can also start lasso selection over selected content when not on a resize handle.

Box-selection hit testing now receives the active box-selection mode, while frame-based generation and exports use calculated bounds and include only elements that strictly intersect the frame and are unframed or belong to that frame.
Production pages now preload the Assistant SemiBold font, which should reduce visible font swapping for text using that weight.
The Preferences controls now include box-selection mode choices of contain and overlap; selecting either updates the editor’s current setting.
Radio-choice controls can show a leading icon and their descriptive heading now truncates to one line when it exceeds the available width, affecting the box-selection and system-theme controls.
qaChecks: Verify a selection box that covers a shape’s geometric bounds but not the outer half-stroke does not select it; the previous behavior selected it.
Check that a box around an arrow’s line but not its attached text does not select the arrow, and that a box enclosing both does select the arrow.
Confirm selecting a frame does not also select its contained elements.
Verify clicking an empty corner inside the rotated element’s axis-aligned bounding box does not select the element or follow its link, while clicking on the rotated element does.
Verify lasso-selection with a boundary crossing the stroke at a shallow angle near its curve midpoint; confirm the stroke is selected when the boundary crosses it.
Check erasing across the same shallow, near-tangent crossing; confirm the stroke is erased where the eraser passes over it.
Verify that opening the drawing with no saved preference uses “contain”: a selection box enclosing an element selects it, while one that only partly overlaps it does not.
Verify that opening the drawing saved with “overlap” retains that mode: a selection box that partly overlaps an element selects it.
Check the frame export in canvas and SVG formats: the exported drawing includes the element that geometrically overlaps the frame.

Verify that with multiple objects selected, moving the pointer just outside their shared bounds but within the added transform-handle spacing shows a move cursor, and dragging there moves the selection rather than starting a lasso.
Check that pressing Alt+Ctrl or Alt+Cmd and starting a drag over selected content, away from resize handles, starts lasso selection.
Confirm that a box-selection drag which only partly overlaps an object follows the inclusion rule of the active box-selection mode.

Verify that generated and exported frame content includes elements whose bounds strictly intersect the frame when they are unframed or assigned to that frame, and excludes the element assigned to another frame.
Check that the element whose bounds only touch the frame edge is excluded from frame content and the frame-only export.
Confirm that text using Assistant SemiBold does not visibly switch from a fallback font to its final appearance after the page first renders.
Verify that the box-selection preference offers contain and overlap, and that selecting each choice moves the selected radio to that choice.
Check that a radio-control heading longer than the available row width stays on one line and is truncated rather than expanding or wrapping the row.
uncertainty: The selection logic supports overlap mode, but no visible control or navigation for activating that mode is supplied.

The supplied evidence does not give exact curve coordinates that fail with 4 iterations but succeed within 10, so the shallow-crossing checks are targeted probes rather than a guaranteed old-versus-new reproducer; no user-facing navigation or current application call using the optional bounds padding was supplied.

The supplied evidence does not establish which boundary-crossing element changes export inclusion compared with the prior behavior, or how a user selects the box-selection mode; confirm the overlap checks against the available product workflow.

report.summary: The release expands and reorganizes URL handling, including parsing, assembly, and query processing.
keyChanges: URL parsing now distinguishes protocol-based URLs from relative paths and preserves the difference between a protocol-based root with and without a final slash.
Repeated non-empty query values are retained in order, while an empty first value is replaced by the next value for the same key.
URL components are decoded when valid and kept unchanged when decoding fails, and path joining adds or removes only the needed slash.

URL assembly encodes path separators and reserved characters according to their component, while query keys and values use different escaping rules; hostnames also preserve pipes and brackets, and a port of 0 is omitted.
An empty string query value produces a key without an equals sign, whereas an empty array value produces a blank query component. The previous behavior cannot be determined from the supplied changes.
URL joining appends relative paths, merges query parameters, and uses the appended URL’s fragment when present, while rejecting appended URLs with a protocol.
URL normalization and string conversion serialize parsed URLs, and supplied query parameters override existing values with matching names.
Credentials are included in URL authority text only when a username or password is present, and each value is percent-encoded.
Repeated query keys are now collected as multiple values instead of the previous last-value-only result, changing what query readers return.
Updating query parameters now passes empty values through URL serialization instead of applying the previous truthiness rule that emitted a bare key; the exact serialized form needs confirmation.
URL normalization and joining now use a different URL-handling path, and normalization no longer reads the old option that returned only the path of an absolute URL.
The package entry point now re-exports parsing, utility, URL, and encoding modules, and a new cleanup capability collapses repeated path slashes while preserving the protocol separator.
A URL is considered absolute when it has a protocol or its path starts with “/”; its full address includes the protocol, authentication, host, and path only when a protocol is present.
Search parameters now include one entry for each array value and one entry for each scalar value, while JSON serialization returns the full address.

report.summary: The release reorganizes and replaces URL-handling utilities, with no identified user-facing behavior change.
keyChanges: URL parsing now recognizes only schemes matching a word-character name followed by ://; the previous parser accepted broader scheme names, so URLs using characters such as + may be treated as paths instead.
Query text is retained as a search string until parsed, and query helpers now parse, merge, and serialize values; when serializing, a numeric value of 0 produces a key without =0.
Parsed URLs are serialized with their path, query, and fragment, with protocol, authentication, and host included when present.
Query strings are now retained as raw search text instead of being converted into decoded parameter entries, changing how empty and repeated values are represented.
New URL accessors expose decoded username, password, hostname, and port values, while encoded authentication omits the colon when the password is empty.

The public entry point now exports encoding, query, URL, and utility modules instead of the former UFO module; the previous query-parameter encoder and parameter helpers are removed, so callers may need to use the reorganized URL and query capabilities.
Previously, an empty-string parameter value serialized as a bare key; the new serialization behavior for that input is not established by the supplied evidence.
The URL object and its constructor are removed, so parsing inputs such as an empty string or a complete URL may no longer be available to its consumers.
URL serialization and appending are also removed; consumers that resolve URLs may be affected because the resolution utility previously constructed and appended URL objects.
URL normalization and multi-part resolution now use the new URL representation; the supplied evidence does not establish how this differs from the previous implementation.
The diff adds query-related imports and type declarations but does not show a runtime behavior change.

report.summary: The release expands logging capabilities with configurable interactive prompts and status messages for browsers and terminals.
keyChanges: Consola instances now accept a prompt handler, and the browser factory supplies native browser dialogs; calling prompts on an instance without a handler throws an unsupported error.

Browser confirmation prompts use the native confirmation dialog, while all other prompt types use a standard text prompt; select and multiselect choices and other prompt options are not passed to the browser dialog.
The browser factory now accepts options, including custom reporters, while retaining the browser reporter by default; the log-level edit changes only TypeScript typing and has no runtime effect.
Confirmation prompts start with “Yes” selected unless an initial value is supplied, and display the chosen answer when submitted.
Text prompts display the placeholder for an empty value, including in the submitted result.
Multi-select prompts, including grouped choices, require at least one selection by default and show an error when submitted empty; option and prompt states have distinct visual indicators.

Instances created through the main entry now receive an environment-appropriate default reporter when none is supplied and include interactive prompts for text, confirmation, single-choice, and multiple-choice input.
String choices in selection prompts are used as both their displayed label and returned value.

Status messages now print a separator and format multiline text with a status marker on the first line and separators on following lines; error, information, step, success, and warning messages use distinct markers.

The selection prompt displays options and their active, submitted, or cancelled state, while the spinner removes up to three trailing periods from its running message and replaces the animation with a completion message when stopped.
Terminal prompts now include password entry with a configurable mask, validation, and distinct submitted, canceled, and error displays.

Grouped prompts run in order; when cancellation occurs and a cancellation handler is supplied, the canceled result is recorded as “canceled,” the handler receives results so far, and later prompts continue.
Terminal notes remove ANSI formatting codes when measuring line widths, while intro, outro, and cancellation messages add formatted status output; symbols also have non-Unicode fallbacks.

report.summary: The release improves how the whiteboard updates and restores drawings during editing and recovery.
keyChanges: Deleting or cutting selected elements now returns the remaining drawing instead of leaving the editor with no returned scene, so verify selected elements disappear while unselected elements remain.
Moving one or all selected elements forward, backward, to the front, or to the back now returns the reordered drawing, so verify the stacking changes and the editor remains usable.
Undo and redo now return the restored drawing snapshot, or null when no snapshot is available; verify that history actions update the drawing and empty history leaves it unchanged.
Clearing selection now returns a copied element list with selections cleared, so verify selection-clearing actions leave the editor usable.
On startup, saved drawing elements and app state are restored separately, so verify a saved drawing appears when the editor opens.
Deleting selected elements and keyboard-driven scene updates now use the updated drawing returned by the operation; undo and redo likewise apply a returned drawing when one is available.
Layer-order changes and pasted styles now replace the drawing elements with updated versions, including recalculated text dimensions after a text style is pasted.
Pasted elements no longer have the copied drawing’s top-left coordinates subtracted, so content copied from an offset position can land away from the paste cursor.
Clicking empty canvas while holding Shift now preserves the current selection; clicking empty canvas without Shift clears it.
Scene updates now use returned drawing lists for selected-item style changes, cutting, and scene loading, so verify those edits appear in the canvas.

The changes affect how drawing-element lists are described to the type checker; hit testing, selection checks, and initial scene contents behave the same at runtime. No QA-visible consequence is established.
Importing a JSON file without an elements array now produces an empty scene instead of leaving the current drawing untouched; malformed JSON is caught and also resolves to an empty scene.
On startup, saved drawing data and saved editor state are now parsed separately, so invalid saved editor state no longer discards otherwise valid drawing elements.

report.summary: The release refines text and drawing appearance controls in the editor, so verify that edits behave consistently.

Element appearance, fill, text, and stroke controls now use the edited element’s value before a shared selection value; verify the controls reflect the item being edited when its value differs from the selection.

Color controls now pass null rather than undefined for an unset color; verify an unset color can still be chosen for an element or the canvas.
The color input and palette now describe an unset color as null rather than undefined; the supplied code shows no change to how either value behaves at runtime.

report.summary: The release improves the editor’s scene statistics experience and how it responds to the current selection and visibility settings.
keyChanges: A new statistics panel is available from the canvas context menu and reports scene element count, rounded dimensions, storage sizes, and details for a single selected element or multiple selected elements.
When an element is being edited, it takes precedence over the current selection as the target for selection-dependent details and controls; otherwise, selected elements remain the target.
Storage sizes use abbreviated units (b, k, M, G), with values rounded to one decimal place and trailing zeroes removed.
Total browser-storage size still sums saved app state, collaboration data, library data, and drawing data; missing entries contribute 0, as before.
The selection helper is renamed, and debounced tasks gain a cancellation method, but the supplied changes do not establish a changed editor workflow.

report.summary: The release improves canvas selection and framed exports, with a new preference for box-selection behavior.
keyChanges: Box selection now accounts for stroke width, attached arrow text, frame-clipped visibility, and outline intersections when overlap mode is requested; selection bounds include their edges.

Pointer targeting for a selected rotated element now tests its rotated bounds rather than its larger axis-aligned bounding rectangle, so empty corners outside the rotated shape should not count as hits.
Freehand strokes now use their absolute-geometry midpoint in center calculations, which can affect geometry-dependent interactions.

When checking intersections against curved free-draw or arrow strokes, the solver can now try up to 10 iterations instead of 4, so some previously missed crossings may now be recognized during selection, erasing, and arrow binding.
New drawings default to box selection mode “contain”; restoring a drawing uses its saved mode when present, otherwise the browser’s saved preference or the default.
Framed PNG and SVG exports now provide the full scene lookup when checking which elements overlap the exported frame.
Frame contents are now determined by intersecting element and frame bounds, affecting Magic Frame generation and frame-only image exports, including PNG and SVG previews or clipboard copies.

Alt+Ctrl or Alt+Command on the shared bounds of selected elements can now start lasso selection instead of dragging, and the shared-bounds hit area is larger; hovering that area without Ctrl or Command now shows a move cursor.
Box-selection calculations now receive the current box-selection mode, so verify selection follows the active mode.
Preferences now includes a box-selection mode that sets the editor value to contain or overlap; the supplied evidence does not define how those modes affect drawing selection.
Radio-choice rows can include an icon, and their titles now use ellipsis when they overflow.

report.summary: The release overhauls URL and query handling, changing the public interface and potentially affecting integrations.
keyChanges: URL parsing now keeps query text separate from the path and recognizes relative inputs directly; schemes containing characters other than word characters, such as a plus sign, are no longer recognized as protocols.
Query parsing collects repeated keys as lists, while combining a new query with an existing URL query replaces values for matching keys.
Query serialization emits only the key for empty, false, or zero values and emits array values as repeated key-value pairs.
Query parsing now retains the search text, including its leading question mark, instead of converting it into decoded key/value entries.
Credential parsing splits at the first colon, so additional colons are not preserved in the password, and encoded credentials omit the colon when the password is empty.
Host parsing now separates hostname and port, but its current pattern may not recognize ordinary numeric ports.

The former URL type and parameter helpers are removed from the public exports, while the new URL and query capabilities are exposed; integrations using the old entry points need to switch to the new interface.
The new query utility merges supplied values over existing query values, so test that updates preserve the URL path while applying the supplied value.

URL construction, path appending, query-parameter handling, and URL serialization for host, credentials, origin, and full address are removed; related URL helper operations depended on this implementation, so confirm those capabilities remain available.
URL normalization and resolution now use the replacement URL representation; the evidence does not establish whether their resulting strings differ from before.
The change adds query-related type declarations, but no runtime behavior change is shown.
